```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: Moein A, Langenhorst J, Kassir N. A Longitudinal Disease
  Progression Model Characterizing Endoscopic Response and Remission in
  Crohn's Disease. J Pharmacokinet Pharmacodyn. 2026.
  doi:10.1007/s10928-026-10042-x
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-026-10042-x> (PMC free full text:
  PMC13356052)
* Supplementary Material 1 is the NONMEM control stream of the final model;
  Supplementary Material 2 holds the baseline tables (S1-S4) and the FREM
  covariate forest plot (Figure S5).

```{r load-model}
mod <- readModelDb("Moein_2026_crohns_sescd")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

There is **no drug, no dose and no ODE** in this model. It describes how the
Simple Endoscopic Score for Crohn's Disease (SES-CD) evolves in placebo-treated
patients, so that a drug effect can later be added on top of it. The source is
a NONMEM `$PRED` model, so the packaged model is purely algebraic in time.

# Population

The analysis set was the 155 patients of the phase 3 BERGAMOT trial
(NCT02394028) who received placebo in the 14-week induction phase and, if they
reached a CDAI-70 clinical response (a decrease of at least 70 points from the
baseline Crohn's Disease Activity Index) at week 14, placebo again in the
52-week maintenance phase; 117 entered maintenance. Patients had
moderately-to-severely active Crohn's disease. At induction baseline
(Tables S2 and S3) the mean age was 36.9 years (range 18-79), mean body weight
70.9 kg (39.7-118.4), 44.5% were female, 65.8% had prior anti-TNF exposure,
the mean CDAI was 324.9 (211-479) and the mean SES-CD 13.6 (4-36). Disease
location was ileum and colon in 62.6%, ileum only in 18.7% and colon only in
18.7%. The data were 6,202 endoscopic subscore observations from ileocolonoscopies
at baseline, end of induction (week 14) and end of maintenance (week 66).

```{r population}
str(mod()$population)
```

# Model structure

SES-CD scores four variables -- size of ulcers, ulcerated surface, affected
surface and presence of narrowings -- each 0-3 in each of five segments (ileum,
right colon, transverse colon, left colon and sigmoid, rectum), giving 20
subscores (items). Each item is a **bounded-integer** ordinal endpoint: a latent
normal value with item location `mean` and dispersion `sd` on the probit scale
is cut at `qnorm(1/4)`, `qnorm(2/4)` and `qnorm(3/4)`, so

$$P(\text{score} = k) = \Phi\!\left(\frac{c_{k+1} - \text{mean}}{\text{sd}}\right) - \Phi\!\left(\frac{c_k - \text{mean}}{\text{sd}}\right), \quad c_0 = -\infty,\; c_4 = +\infty.$$

For subject *i* and item *j* in segment *s* (Moein 2026 Equations 1 and 2):

* `mean_ij = probitbase_j + etaprobitbase_s,i + pbo_i`, where the baseline
  random effect is shared by the four items of a segment;
* `sd_ij = exp(lsd_j + etalsd_i)`, one dispersion random effect shared by all
  20 items;
* `pbo_i = (pmax + etapmax_i) * (1 - exp(-log(2) / thalf_pbo * t))`, the single
  latent placebo trajectory that shifts every item equally (the IRT link).

A negative `pmax` lowers every item location, i.e. improves the endoscopy. The
model also returns each item's expected subscore `escore_<segment>_<item>` and
their sum `escore_sescd`.

The control stream also contains a logistic **dropout** submodel for the end of
induction, `prob_dropout = expit(logitp_dropout + e_score_cdai_delta_p_dropout *
SCORE_CDAI_DELTA)`, the probability that a subject does not enter maintenance
given the change in CDAI from baseline at week 14. The authors used it to decide
which simulated subjects enter maintenance in their visual predictive checks.

# Source trace

| Element | Value in the model | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 20 item baselines `probitbase_<segment>_<item>` | Table 1 'BASE' rows | Table 1; control stream THETA(1, 3, 5, ..., 39) |
| 20 item dispersions `lsd_<segment>_<item>` | log of Table 1 'SD' rows | Table 1; control stream THETA(2, 4, ..., 40) |
| `pmax` | -0.329 | Table 1 'R MaxPL'; THETA(41) |
| `lthalf_pbo` | log(13.8 week) | Table 1 'T50 PL'; THETA(42) |
| `logitp_dropout` | 4.36 | Table 1 'Intercept Dropout End of Induction'; THETA(43) |
| `e_score_cdai_delta_p_dropout` | 0.0607 per CDAI point | Table 1 'Slope Dropout End of Induction'; THETA(44) |
| `etaprobitbase_ileum` ... `_rectum` | 0.712, 0.521, 1.07, 0.923, 1.11 | Table 1 'IIVBASE' rows (variances); $OMEGA 1-5 |
| `etalsd` | 0.0923 | Table 1 'IIVSD IRT'; $OMEGA 6, exponential on SD |
| `etapmax` | 0.648 | Table 1 'IIV RMaxPL'; $OMEGA 7, additive on RMaxPL |
| Placebo trajectory | `(pmax + eta) * (1 - exp(-log(2)/thalf * t))` | Equation 1; control stream `PLEFF` |
| Item location and dispersion | `mean = BASE + eta_segment + Response`, `SD = SD_j * exp(eta)` | Equation 2; control stream `BASE`, `SD` |
| Cut points | `qnorm(1:3 / 4)` = -0.6745, 0, 0.6745 | control stream `CO1`-`CO3` |
| Category probabilities | normal CDF differences | control stream `P0`-`P3` |
| Dropout logit | `INT + SLOPE * CEOICDAI` | control stream `P_EOIDROP` |
| Score-scale transform | `3 * Phi(E)` | Equation 3 (diagnostic only) |

The individual Table 1 values and their control-stream counterparts are listed
next to every `ini()` line of the model file.

# Reproducing the Table 1 score-scale column

Table 1 prints, beside each bounded-integer estimate, an "approximate mean
SES-CD subscore" obtained with Equation 3, `3 * Phi(E)`. Recomputing it from
the packaged baselines checks the transcription of all 20 locations. The
reported score-scale value of `pmax` (-0.220) is the mean over the 20 items of
`3 * (Phi(BASE + RMaxPL) - Phi(BASE))`, which the paper rounds to a reduction of
about 4.4 points in total SES-CD.

```{r score-scale}
ini_df <- ui$iniDf
base_df <- ini_df[grepl("^probitbase_", ini_df$name), c("name", "est")]
table1_score_scale <- c(
  1.44, 1.28, 1.409, 0.312, 0.879, 0.736, 0.821, 0.017, 0.503, 0.414,
  0.529, 0.002, 0.933, 0.752, 0.910, 0.025, 0.595, 0.527, 0.672, 0.007
)
score_scale <- base_df |>
  mutate(
    computed = 3 * pnorm(est),
    table1 = table1_score_scale,
    difference = computed - table1
  )
knitr::kable(score_scale, digits = 4)

pmax_val <- ini_df$est[ini_df$name == "pmax"]
pmax_score_scale <- mean(3 * (pnorm(base_df$est + pmax_val) - pnorm(base_df$est)))
c(pmax_score_scale = pmax_score_scale, total_sescd_change = 20 * pmax_score_scale)

stopifnot(
  max(abs(score_scale$difference)) < 0.0015,
  abs(pmax_score_scale - (-0.220)) < 0.0015
)
```

# Typical-subject trajectory

```{r typical}
items <- base_df$name |> sub(pattern = "^probitbase_", replacement = "")
item_label <- function(x) {
  seg <- c(
    ileum = "Ileum", rcolon = "Right colon", tcolon = "Transverse colon",
    lcolon = "Left colon", rectum = "Rectum"
  )
  var <- c(
    ulcersize = "Size of ulcers", ulcerated = "Ulcerated surface",
    affected = "Affected surface", narrowing = "Presence of narrowings"
  )
  parts <- strsplit(x, "_", fixed = TRUE)
  vapply(parts, function(p) paste0(var[[p[2]]], ": ", seg[[p[1]]]), "")
}

ev_typ <- data.frame(
  id = 1, time = seq(0, 462, by = 7), evid = 0,
  cmt = "sescd_ileum_ulcersize", SCORE_CDAI_DELTA = 0
)
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod, which = "omega"), ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame")

ggplot(typ, aes(time / 7, escore_sescd)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time since first dose (weeks)",
    y = "Expected total SES-CD",
    title = "Typical placebo patient (all random effects at zero)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The typical patient's placebo response reaches about a fifth of its maximum by
week 5 and half of it at 13.8 weeks.

# Virtual cohort and simulation

The simulation reproduces the paper's visual predictive checks: 100 replicate
trials of 155 placebo patients, each with endoscopy at baseline, week 14 (end of
induction, day 98) and week 66 (end of maintenance, day 462). Only one
observation record per visit is solved: every item's category probabilities
come back as columns of that record, and the 20 subscores are then drawn from
them in R. This is equivalent to solving one record per item, at a twentieth of
the cost.

The SES-CD part of the model does not depend on the CDAI change, so the
dropout covariate is set to 0 here and is examined separately below.

```{r simulate}
n_sub <- 155
n_trials <- 100
visits <- c(0, 98, 462)
ev <- expand.grid(time = visits, id = seq_len(n_sub)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0, cmt = "sescd_ileum_ulcersize", SCORE_CDAI_DELTA = 0) |>
  arrange(id, time)

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261025)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, nStud = n_trials, returnType = "data.frame")
```

Each simulated subscore is drawn from its four category probabilities. Two
draw schemes are compared:

* **independent**: one uniform draw per item and visit, which is what rxode2's
  ordinal endpoints (`sescd_<segment>_<item> ~ c(p0, p1, p2)`) do;
* **authors' scheme**: the simulation block of the published control stream
  draws one uniform number `R1` per subject (`IF(NEWIND.NE.2) CALL RANDOM(2,R)`)
  and reuses it for every item and every visit of that subject.

```{r draw}
long <- sim |>
  select(sim.id, id, time, starts_with("p0_"), starts_with("p1_"), starts_with("p2_")) |>
  pivot_longer(
    -c(sim.id, id, time),
    names_to = c(".value", "item"),
    names_pattern = "^(p[012])_(.*)$"
  ) |>
  mutate(c0 = p0, c1 = p0 + p1, c2 = p0 + p1 + p2)

set.seed(20261025)
u_subject <- sim |>
  distinct(sim.id, id) |>
  mutate(u_subj = runif(n()))
long <- long |>
  left_join(u_subject, by = c("sim.id", "id")) |>
  mutate(
    u_ind = runif(n()),
    score_ind = (u_ind > c0) + (u_ind > c1) + (u_ind > c2),
    score_auth = (u_subj > c0) + (u_subj > c1) + (u_subj > c2)
  )
```

# Replicate Figure 3 -- mean subscores over time

Replicates Figure 3 of Moein 2026 (mean SES-CD subscore by item over time with
the 90% interval of 100 simulated trial means). The black points are the
observed baseline (week 0) and week-14 means of Table S4; the week-14 values
are those of the 117 patients who entered maintenance.

```{r fig3, fig.height = 9}
table_s4 <- data.frame(
  item = items,
  wk0 = c(
    1.42, 1.27, 1.44, 0.66, 1.02, 0.81, 0.94, 0.31, 0.81, 0.65,
    0.85, 0.10, 1.06, 0.87, 1.05, 0.12, 0.83, 0.72, 0.88, 0.06
  ),
  wk14 = c(
    1.44, 1.29, 1.38, 0.64, 0.77, 0.62, 0.76, 0.24, 0.60, 0.50,
    0.63, 0.09, 0.83, 0.67, 0.84, 0.13, 0.61, 0.53, 0.69, 0.08
  )
)
obs_s4 <- table_s4 |>
  pivot_longer(c(wk0, wk14), names_to = "visit", values_to = "mean_obs") |>
  mutate(week = ifelse(visit == "wk0", 0, 14), label = item_label(item))

trial_means <- long |>
  group_by(sim.id, time, item) |>
  summarise(m = mean(score_ind), .groups = "drop")
band <- trial_means |>
  group_by(time, item) |>
  summarise(
    lo = quantile(m, 0.05), med = median(m), hi = quantile(m, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(week = time / 7, label = item_label(item))

ggplot(band, aes(week)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(aes(y = med), colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_point(data = obs_s4, aes(y = mean_obs), colour = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~label, ncol = 4) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 2)) +
  labs(x = "Time since first dose (weeks)", y = "SES-CD subscore (0-3)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 8)
```

```{r baseline-table}
baseline_cmp <- band |>
  filter(time == 0) |>
  left_join(table_s4, by = "item") |>
  transmute(
    Item = label,
    "Simulated median" = med,
    "Simulated 90% interval" = sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", lo, hi),
    "Observed (Table S4)" = wk0
  )
knitr::kable(baseline_cmp, digits = 2)
```

# Replicate Figure 4 -- endoscopic response and remission

Endoscopic response is a reduction of at least 50% from the baseline total
SES-CD and remission a total SES-CD of 0-2 (FDA 2022 guidance), assessed at the
end of induction (week 14) and the end of maintenance (week 66). Figure 4 of
Moein 2026 prints the observed rates (17%, 41%, 8% and 14%) and the median
misprediction of the simulations (+3%, 0%, +2% and +9%), i.e. simulated medians
of about 20%, 41%, 10% and 23%. The maintenance rates in the paper are among
patients who entered maintenance; in this model entry depends only on the CDAI
change, which is independent of the latent SES-CD trajectory, so it does not
alter the expected maintenance-phase SES-CD distribution and every simulated
subject is carried to week 66.

```{r fig4}
totals <- long |>
  group_by(sim.id, id, time) |>
  summarise(
    independent = sum(score_ind),
    authors = sum(score_auth),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(c(independent, authors), names_to = "scheme", values_to = "total")

endpoints <- totals |>
  group_by(sim.id, id, scheme) |>
  mutate(baseline = total[time == 0]) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  mutate(
    response = baseline > 0 & total <= 0.5 * baseline,
    remission = total <= 2
  )

rates <- endpoints |>
  group_by(scheme, sim.id, time) |>
  summarise(
    response = 100 * mean(response),
    remission = 100 * mean(remission),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(c(response, remission), names_to = "endpoint", values_to = "pct") |>
  group_by(scheme, time, endpoint) |>
  summarise(
    median = median(pct), lo = quantile(pct, 0.05), hi = quantile(pct, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(phase = ifelse(time == 98, "End of induction", "End of maintenance"))

published <- data.frame(
  endpoint = c("response", "response", "remission", "remission"),
  phase = rep(c("End of induction", "End of maintenance"), 2),
  observed = c(17, 41, 8, 14),
  paper_sim_median = c(17 + 3, 41 + 0, 8 + 2, 14 + 9)
)
fig4_cmp <- rates |>
  left_join(published, by = c("endpoint", "phase")) |>
  arrange(endpoint, phase, scheme)
fig4_cmp |>
  transmute(
    Endpoint = endpoint, Visit = phase, "Draw scheme" = scheme,
    "Simulated median (%)" = median,
    "Simulated 90% interval (%)" = sprintf("%.1f-%.1f", lo, hi),
    "Paper simulated median (%)" = paper_sim_median,
    "Observed (%)" = observed
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

ggplot(fig4_cmp, aes(scheme, median)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi)) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = observed), colour = "red", linetype = 2) +
  facet_grid(endpoint ~ phase, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Draw scheme", y = "Patients (%)",
    caption = "Red dashed line: observed rate printed in Figure 4."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

With the authors' draw scheme the simulated rates reproduce the simulated
medians the paper prints in Figure 4 at both visits, including the
over-prediction of remission at the end of maintenance (about 23% simulated
against 14% observed) that the authors report. The draw scheme matters for these
binary endpoints because they depend on the *sum* of 20 subscores: reusing one
uniform number for all items of a subject makes the subscores move together and
widens the spread of the total. The item means of Figure 3 are the same under
either scheme.

# End-of-induction dropout submodel

```{r dropout}
cdai_grid <- data.frame(
  id = 1, time = 98, evid = 0, cmt = "dropout",
  SCORE_CDAI_DELTA = seq(-250, 50, by = 5)
) |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n()))
# rxSolve returns the covariate column alongside the outputs.
drop_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod, which = "omega"), cdai_grid, returnType = "data.frame")

ggplot(drop_typ, aes(SCORE_CDAI_DELTA, prob_dropout)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = -70, linetype = 2) +
  labs(
    x = "CDAI change from baseline at week 14 (points)",
    y = "Probability of not entering maintenance",
    caption = "Dashed line: the CDAI-70 response required to enter maintenance."
  ) +
  theme_bw()

p_ini <- setNames(ini_df$est, ini_df$name)
cdai_half <- -p_ini[["logitp_dropout"]] / p_ini[["e_score_cdai_delta_p_dropout"]]
cdai_half
stopifnot(abs(cdai_half - (-70)) < 5)
```

The dropout probability is one half at a CDAI change of about -72 points,
reproducing the protocol rule that only CDAI-70 responders continued placebo
into maintenance.

# FREM covariates on the maximum placebo response

The covariate analysis used the full random effects model (FREM). It reports
relative changes in RMaxPL at the 5th and 95th percentiles of each covariate,
not a parametric covariate model, so none of these effects is coded in the
packaged model; they are recorded in its `covariatesDataExcluded` metadata.
Values transcribed from Figure S5 (median and 90% CI of the RMaxPL ratio to the
reference subject):

| Covariate | Value | RMaxPL ratio [90% CI] |
|---|---|---|
| C-reactive protein | 75.86 / 0.59 mg/L | 0.53 [-0.19, 0.95] / 1.5 [1.1, 2.4] |
| Fecal calprotectin | 8511 / 66.07 ug/g | 0.40 [-0.15, 0.89] / 1.5 [1.1, 2.1] |
| Anti-TNF status | TNF-naive / prior TNF | 1.6 [1.3, 2.1] / 0.69 [0.41, 0.83] |
| Body weight | 102 / 49 kg | 1.1 [1.0, 1.2] / 0.91 [0.79, 0.97] |
| Albumin | 48.98 / 33.11 g/L | 1.0 [1.0, 1.1] / 0.96 [0.90, 1.0] |
| White blood cells | 14.13 / 4.27 x10^9/L | 1.0 [0.93, 1.2] / 0.96 [0.75, 1.1] |
| Neutrophils | 11.48 / 2.75 x10^9/L | 1.1 [0.89, 1.3] / 0.93 [0.71, 1.1] |
| Baseline SES-CD | 25.70 / 4.68 | 0.85 [0.63, 1.0] / 1.2 [0.94, 1.4] |
| Baseline CDAI | 457 / 234 | 0.96 [0.87, 1.0] / 1.0 [0.97, 1.1] |
| Smoking | current / previous / never | 1.2 [0.84, 1.6] / 1.3 [1.0, 1.9] / 0.78 [0.50, 0.95] |
| Disease location | ileum and colon / colon / ileum | 0.99 [0.76, 1.2] / 1.1 [0.64, 1.5] / 0.93 [0.42, 1.5] |

A ratio below 1 means a smaller placebo response.

# Validation

There is no drug exposure in this model, so there is no NCA; PKNCA is loaded
only to keep the article set uniform. The checks are:

* the Table 1 score-scale column and the -0.220 RMaxPL score-scale value are
  reproduced to the printed precision (above);
* the dropout logit crosses one half at the CDAI-70 entry rule (above);
* the simulated baseline item means match the observed means of Table S4;
* the simulated response and remission rates at both visits bracket the
  paper's own simulated medians.

```{r validation}
base_check <- band |>
  filter(time == 0) |>
  left_join(table_s4, by = "item") |>
  mutate(diff = med - wk0)
summary(base_check$diff)

fig4_cmp |>
  filter(scheme == "authors") |>
  select(endpoint, phase, median, lo, hi, paper_sim_median, observed)

stopifnot(
  # Structural: a mis-transcribed baseline or a wrong cut point shifts the
  # simulated item means by tenths of a point.
  abs(median(base_check$diff)) < 0.1,
  quantile(abs(base_check$diff), 0.9) < 0.25,
  # The paper's simulated medians (both visits) lie inside the 90%
  # interval of this simulation under the authors' draw scheme.
  all(with(
    filter(fig4_cmp, scheme == "authors"),
    paper_sim_median >= lo & paper_sim_median <= hi
  ))
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Final estimates.** All values come from Table 1. The control stream
  `$THETA`/`$OMEGA` records carry the same estimates; five thetas and four
  omegas differ in the last printed digit (for example THETA(1) -0.0503 versus
  Table 1 -0.050, and $OMEGA(1) 0.713 versus 0.712). Table 1 is used.
* **IIV values are variances.** Table 1 prints the IIV estimates without a
  scale; they agree with the control-stream `$OMEGA` records, which are
  variances, and are used as such.
* **Time unit.** The control stream evaluates the placebo trajectory in weeks
  (`TSFDD / 7`). The packaged model takes time in days and divides by 7
  internally; `thalf_pbo` stays in weeks as printed.
* **Ordinal likelihood.** Each SES-CD subscore is an rxode2 ordinal endpoint
  `~ c(p0, p1, p2)`, which reproduces the control stream's categorical
  likelihood (`Y = P0`, ..., `Y = P3`). rxode2 numbers the categories 1-4, so
  simulated category k is subscore k - 1. The dropout endpoint is a two-category
  ordinal endpoint (category 1 = continues, category 2 = drops out).
* **Simulation draw scheme.** The control stream's simulation block reuses one
  uniform number per subject for every item and visit; rxode2's ordinal
  endpoints draw independently per record. Both are shown above. The item means
  are unaffected; the response and remission rates depend on the choice.
* **Dropout covariate.** The CDAI change at the end of induction is the
  control-stream column `CEOICDAI`, encoded as `SCORE_CDAI_DELTA` (CDAI at
  week 14 minus baseline). Its distribution is not reported, so the simulations
  carry every subject to week 66; because the covariate does not enter the
  SES-CD part of the model, this leaves the simulated maintenance-phase
  subscore distribution unchanged.
* **Baseline eligibility.** BERGAMOT enrolled patients with a minimum baseline
  SES-CD, and the observed minimum was 4. Simulated baselines are not
  truncated, as in the paper's own simulations, so some simulated patients
  start in remission.
* **Unused active-treatment terms.** The control stream contains commented-out
  `ACTMAX`/`ACT50` placeholders for a future drug effect and a treatment
  indicator that is 1 for every analysed (placebo) patient; neither is part of
  the estimated model and neither is packaged.
* **FREM covariates.** Covariate effects on RMaxPL are available only as the
  Figure S5 forest plot and are not coded in the model (see above).
